item.text:
## 1B.3 Research Note: Lula, Brazil, 2024

**Bottom line:** The 2024 record points **yes, overall** on command-and-control discipline and accident-prevention safeguards. I found multiple 2024 indicators of formal nuclear safety governance, emergency readiness, independent oversight, and automatic fail-safe behavior. I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence that Lula weakened custody or bypassed safeguards.

### Accepted claims

- **Claim:** Brazil maintained an active emergency-response and security-fighting exercise regime around its nuclear plants in 2024, with no public involvement in the partial drill.
  - **Title:** [Eletronuclear clarifies information about emergency drills and nuclear security](https://www.eletronuclear.gov.br/Imprensa-e-Midias/Paginas/eletronuclear-esclarece-informacoes-sobre-simulados-de-emergencia-e-seguranca-nuclear.aspx)
  - **Publisher:** Eletronuclear
  - **Date:** May 9, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.eletronuclear.gov.br/Imprensa-e-Midias/Paginas/eletronuclear-esclarece-informacoes-sobre-simulados-de-emergencia-e-seguranca-nuclear.aspx
  - **Claim-level summary:** The company said the 2024 drill would be a partial exercise, without population involvement, and that the full integrated exercise is normally supervised by the Presidency-linked GSI and coordinated by state civil defense. This is strong evidence of disciplined emergency-preparedness procedures.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.3`

- **Claim:** Brazil’s nuclear safety regulator and the IAEA publicly emphasized close cooperation in 2024.
  - **Title:** [IAEA recognizes CNEN's "crucial" role in nuclear technology development in Brazil](https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/aiea-reconhece-papel-crucial-da-cnen-no-desenvolvimento-da-tecnologia-nuclear-no-brasil)
  - **Publisher:** Comissão Nacional de Energia Nuclear
  - **Date:** June 24, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/aiea-reconhece-papel-crucial-da-cnen-no-desenvolvimento-da-tecnologia-nuclear-no-brasil
  - **Claim-level summary:** CNEN said IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi highlighted indispensable CNEN cooperation in Brazil. This supports a picture of regulated, externally engaged oversight rather than loose or ad hoc custody.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.3`

- **Claim:** Brazil’s nuclear regulator was participating in international regulatory review work in 2024.
  - **Title:** [Brazil participates in unprecedented IAEA self-assessment in Vienna, contributing to strengthening global nuclear safety](https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/brasil-participa-de-autoavaliacao-inedita-da-aiea-em-viena-contribuindo-para-o-fortalecimento-da-seguranca-nuclear-global)
  - **Publisher:** Comissão Nacional de Energia Nuclear
  - **Date:** October 3, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/brasil-participa-de-autoavaliacao-inedita-da-aiea-em-viena-contribuindo-para-o-fortalecimento-da-seguranca-nuclear-global
  - **Claim-level summary:** Brazil took part in an IAEA regulatory self-assessment process, which is evidence of institutional attention to safety rules, procedures, and review culture.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.3`

- **Claim:** The federal government explicitly highlighted legal and financial mechanisms for nuclear accident liability, decommissioning, and spent fuel storage.
  - **Title:** [Nuclear plants are safe and sustainable](https://www.gov.br/secom/pt-br/fatos/brasil-contra-fake/noticias/2024/10/usinas-nucleares-sao-seguras-e-sustentaveis)
  - **Publisher:** Secretaria de Comunicação Social
  - **Date:** October 9, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/secom/pt-br/fatos/brasil-contra-fake/noticias/2024/10/usinas-nucleares-sao-seguras-e-sustentaveis
  - **Claim-level summary:** The government said operators must carry accident insurance, maintain a decommissioning fund, and store spent fuel at the plant in a controlled facility. That is direct custody-and-safety evidence.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.3`

- **Claim:** CNEN approved a long-term operating extension for Angra 1 only after a rigorous safety review.
  - **Title:** [CNEN authorizes extension of Angra 1 operation for another 20 years](https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/cnen-autoriza-extensao-da-operacao-de-angra-1-por-mais-20-anos/)
  - **Publisher:** Comissão Nacional de Energia Nuclear
  - **Date:** November 22, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/cnen-autoriza-extensao-da-operacao-de-angra-1-por-mais-20-anos/
  - **Claim-level summary:** CNEN said the extension followed a rigorous technical and safety evaluation and would apply only if strict safety criteria continued to be met. This is a clear sign of disciplined accident-prevention oversight.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.3`

- **Claim:** A December 2024 Angra 2 incident was contained automatically and treated as non-nuclear, with no risk to the public.
  - **Title:** [Official note - Event at Angra 2 Nuclear Power Plant](https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/nota-oficial)
  - **Publisher:** Comissão Nacional de Energia Nuclear
  - **Date:** December 22, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.gov.br/cnen/pt-br/assunto/ultimas-noticias/nota-oficial
  - **Claim-level summary:** CNEN said a small fire in thermal insulation on a turbine component was controlled by the plant fire brigade, the reactor was reduced in power as a precaution, and there was no risk to workers, the environment, or the public. This is useful evidence that safeguards and response procedures functioned.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.3`

- **Claim:** A March 2024 Angra 1 sensor fault triggered an automatic preventive shutdown, showing fail-safe behavior.
  - **Title:** [Angra 1 nuclear plant is temporarily shut down after sensor failure](https://economia.uol.com.br/noticias/reuters/2024/03/26/usina-nuclear-angra-1-e-desligada-temporariamente-apos-falha-em-sensor.htm)
  - **Publisher:** Reuters via UOL
  - **Date:** March 26, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://economia.uol.com.br/noticias/reuters/2024/03/26/usina-nuclear-angra-1-e-desligada-temporariamente-apos-falha-em-sensor.htm
  - **Claim-level summary:** Reuters reported that Angra 1 shut down automatically after a sensor error during maintenance, with the operator saying there was no nuclear risk to the environment or nearby population. That supports functioning safety interlocks and conservative operating discipline.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.3`

### Cautionary evidence

- **Claim:** Brazil’s nuclear plants still experienced operational incidents in 2024, even if they were contained.
  - **Title:** [Angra 2 is disconnected from the National Interconnected System](https://www.eletronuclear.gov.br/Imprensa-e-Midias/Paginas/Angra-2-%C3%A9-desconectada-do-Sistema-Interligado-Nacional.aspx)
  - **Publisher:** Eletronuclear
  - **Date:** December 22, 2024
  - **Recoverable URL:** https://www.eletronuclear.gov.br/Imprensa-e-Midias/Paginas/Angra-2-%C3%A9-desconectada-do-Sistema-Interligado-Nacional.aspx
  - **Claim-level summary:** The plant entered an unusual-event state after a non-nuclear fire in turbine insulation and had to be taken off the grid temporarily. This does not show weakened safeguards, but it is a reminder that operational risk remained present in 2024.
  - **Question IDs:** `1B.3`

### Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that Lula or his government:
- relaxed custody or access controls,
- bypassed safety procedures,
- weakened emergency-preparedness routines,
- or tolerated unsafe nuclear handling.

The evidence available for 2024 is mostly the opposite: routine drills, regulator involvement, liability/decommissioning mechanisms, IAEA-linked oversight, and automatic shutdown/containment behavior during incidents.
